questions.question:
Secure the Docker daemon of the worker node `{{NODE02}}` (connect with `ssh {{NODE02}}`; the daemon runs as the service `docker`).

1. Remove the user `developer` from the group `docker`. Do not remove the user from any other group.
2. Reconfigure and restart the Docker daemon so that the socket `/var/run/docker.sock` is owned by the group `root`.
3. Reconfigure and restart the Docker daemon so that it does not listen on any TCP port.

After completing your work, make sure the Kubernetes cluster is healthy.

verification.description: The user developer is not a member of the group docker
developer keeps all its other groups (credited once removed from docker)
The restarted Docker daemon serves /var/run/docker.sock with the group root
The Docker daemon listens on no TCP port, answers on its socket, and the cluster is healthy

questions.question:
A security audit found a Deployment that handles ServiceAccount tokens improperly, in the namespace `monitoring`.

1. Modify the existing ServiceAccount `stats-monitor-sa` so that it does not automount API credentials.
2. Modify the existing Deployment `stats-monitor` so that a ServiceAccount token is injected and mounted at `/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token`. Use a **projected volume named `token`** and mount it **read-only** (`readOnly: true` on the volume mount).

The manifest of the Deployment is in `/tmp/exam/mhagou-009-q2/deployment.yaml` (apply it again after your change).

verification.description: ServiceAccount stats-monitor-sa does not automount API credentials
The Deployment projects the token (volume token) read-only at the required path
The rolled-out Pods expose a valid token of stats-monitor-sa from a projected volume

questions.question:
A Role bound to the ServiceAccount of a Pod grants overly permissive permissions. In the namespace `database` the Pod `web-pod` runs with the ServiceAccount `test-sa`. Reduce the permissions:

1. Edit the existing Role that is bound to `test-sa` so that it only allows the verb `get`, only on resources of type `pods`.
2. Create a new Role named `test-role-2` in the namespace `database` that only allows the verb `update`, only on resources of type `statefulsets`.
3. Create a RoleBinding named `test-role-2-binding` that binds `test-role-2` to `test-sa`.

verification.description: The Role bound to test-sa (test-role-1) allows only get on pods
Role test-role-2 allows only update on statefulsets
test-role-2 is bound to the ServiceAccount of web-pod and allows only update on statefulsets

questions.question:
A suspicious process is running inside a container of the namespace `incident-lab` on the worker node `{{NODE01}}` (`ssh {{NODE01}}`).

Using Falco, monitor the process activity of the containers of that node for at least **40 seconds** and identify the suspicious process.

Create an incident report `/tmp/exam/mhagou-009-q4/report` on `{{NODE01}}`. It must contain the observed process events in CSV format with exactly three fields per line and **no header**:

`timestamp,uid,processName`

The report must contain the suspicious process and the UID under which it was executed. Do not stop or remove the containers.

verification.description: The report is CSV with exactly timestamp,uid,processName per line, without header
All timestamps of the report are valid
The report contains the suspicious process with the UID it ran under
The events cover the requested observation time

questions.question:
Enable audit logging on the control plane (`{{CONTROL_PLANE}}`). Enable the log backend and make sure that:

1. the logs are stored at `/var/log/kubernetes/logs.txt`,
2. the log files are retained for **5** days,
3. at most **10** old audit log files are retained.

A basic policy is provided at `/etc/kubernetes/logpolicy/audit-policy.yaml` on the control plane. It only specifies what **not** to log. Edit and extend it so that it also logs:

1. changes to `nodes` at the `RequestResponse` level,
2. the request body of changes to `persistentvolumeclaims` in the namespace `frontend`,
3. changes to `configmaps` and `secrets` in all namespaces at the `Metadata` level.

Also add a catch-all rule that logs all other requests at the `Metadata` level. Apply the modified policy: the API server must use it, and it must stay healthy.

verification.description: kube-apiserver uses the policy file and logs to /var/log/kubernetes/logs.txt
Audit log retention: 5 days and 10 old files
Node changes are logged at RequestResponse
The request body of PersistentVolumeClaim changes in frontend is logged
ConfigMap and Secret changes in all namespaces are logged at Metadata
All other requests are logged at Metadata
The do-not-log rules of the base policy are still effective

questions.question:
A container image scanner is set up on the cluster, but it is not yet integrated into the cluster configuration. When complete, the scanner must scan the images of new Pods and reject vulnerable ones.

Given an incomplete configuration in the directory `/etc/kubernetes/epconfig` of the control plane (`{{CONTROL_PLANE}}`: `admission-config.yaml`, `webhook.kubeconfig` and the CA `webhook.pem`) and a functional container image scanner with the HTTPS endpoint `https://wakanda.local:8081/image_policy`:

1. Enable the necessary plugins to create an image policy.
2. Validate the control configuration and change it to an **implicit deny**.
3. Edit the configuration to point to the provided HTTPS endpoint correctly.

The API server must be healthy afterwards. For your tests: the scanner treats the image `nginx:1.16` as vulnerable and accepts `registry.k8s.io/pause:3.10` (the namespace `scanner-lab` is yours for server-side dry-runs).

verification.description: The ImagePolicyWebhook plugin is enabled with an admission configuration file
The active configuration is an implicit deny (defaultAllow false)
The webhook kubeconfig points to https://wakanda.local:8081/image_policy
A Pod with the vulnerable image is rejected by the scanner
An approved image is still admitted (credited once the vulnerable image is rejected)

questions.question:
An Nginx Pod named `nginx` runs in the namespace `web-tier` on the worker node `{{NODE02}}` (`ssh {{NODE02}}`). It has two containers: `nginx` and `log-agent`.

Using Falco, analyse the behaviour of the **`nginx` container** for at least **20 seconds**, with filters that detect newly spawned and executed processes in that container.

Store the incident file at `/tmp/exam/mhagou-009-q7/falco-incident.txt` on `{{NODE02}}`, one detected incident per line in exactly this format (brackets included):

`[timestamp],[uid],[processName]`

Only processes executed in the `nginx` container may be in the file (not those of `log-agent`), and the file must contain only these records.

verification.description: One [timestamp],[uid],[processName] record per line
The processes executed in the nginx container are in the report
The processes of the other container of the Pod are not in the report
The observation lasted long enough and happened during the exam

A service is listening on port 389 on the worker node `{{NODE01}}` (`ssh {{NODE01}}`).

Find the process-id of the process of the service, store the names of all its open files in `/tmp/exam/mhagou-009-q8/files.txt` on `{{NODE01}}`, and delete the binary of the service.

verification.description: The names of the open files of the service were saved on {{NODE01}}
The binary of the service was deleted

questions.question:
Create a user named `john` that authenticates with a client certificate:

1. Generate a private key and a Certificate Signing Request for `john` (`CN=john`), create the CertificateSigningRequest in the cluster and approve it. Fetch the signed certificate and save it to `/tmp/exam/mhagou-009-q9/john.crt`.
2. In the namespace `john` create a Role named `john-role` that allows listing `pods` and `secrets`.
3. Create a RoleBinding named `john-role-binding` in the namespace `john` that attaches the Role `john-role` to the user `john`.
4. Verify the permissions with `kubectl auth can-i`.

verification.description: A valid CertificateSigningRequest for CN=john exists
The CSR of john is approved
The signed certificate of john is saved in john.crt
Role john-role grants list on pods and secrets
RoleBinding john-role-binding binds john-role to the user john
john can list pods and secrets in the namespace john

questions.question: In the namespace `testing` create a NetworkPolicy named `deny-all` that denies all traffic of type Ingress and Egress for every Pod of the namespace.

verification.description: NetworkPolicy deny-all selects all Pods, isolates ingress and egress and allows nothing
No Pod can reach the Pod server (same or other namespace)
The Pods of testing cannot open connections nor resolve DNS names

questions.question:
Harden a container configuration. The files are in `/tmp/exam/mhagou-009-q11/`: review the existing `Dockerfile` and `deployment.yaml` (a Pod manifest) and improve their security configuration.

1. Modify the `Dockerfile` so that:
   - the Ubuntu base image is pinned to an explicit release tag or an immutable digest instead of an unpinned image;
   - the container runs as the user `test-user` (UID 5487) instead of root.
2. Modify `deployment.yaml` so that:
   - the container runs as UID 5487;
   - the container does not run in privileged mode.

Do not add, remove or modify any other Dockerfile instruction or manifest setting.

verification.description: The Ubuntu base image is pinned to an explicit release tag or digest
The Dockerfile selects test-user (UID 5487) instead of root
No other Dockerfile instruction was changed (credited once base and user are fixed)
The container of the manifest runs as UID 5487
The container of the manifest is not privileged
No other setting of the manifest was changed (credited once uid and privileged are fixed)

questions.question:
The API server of the kubeadm cluster (control plane `{{CONTROL_PLANE}}`) has been configured to allow unauthenticated access. Secure it:

- **Forbid anonymous authentication**: requests without credentials to the API endpoints (`/api`, `/apis`, `/version`, ...) must be answered with HTTP 401. The kubelet probes the API server's `/livez` and `/readyz` endpoints **without credentials**, so these health endpoints must keep answering unauthenticated requests and the kube-apiserver Pod must stay Ready. Use the structured **AuthenticationConfiguration** (`--authentication-config` in the static Pod manifest `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml`; make the file available inside the Pod).
- Use the authorization modes `Node,RBAC`.
- Enable the `NodeRestriction` admission controller.
- Make sure the API server remains available after the changes.

Finally, remove the ClusterRoleBinding `system:anonymous`.

verification.description: The kube-apiserver uses an AuthenticationConfiguration that disables anonymous access or limits it to the health endpoints
Requests without credentials to the API endpoints are answered with HTTP 401
The health endpoints stay anonymous and the kube-apiserver Pod stays Ready (credited with the change)
Authorization modes Node,RBAC and the NodeRestriction admission plugin
The ClusterRoleBinding system:anonymous was removed

questions.question:
In the namespace `registry-gate` Pods must not use mutable image references. Use a **ValidatingAdmissionPolicy** to reject, in that namespace only, every Pod that uses an image with the tag `latest` or an image without any tag or digest.

- Create the ValidatingAdmissionPolicy `deny-latest-tag` and the ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding `deny-latest-tag-binding` that applies it to the namespace `registry-gate` and **denies** the requests that violate it.
- Pods whose images are pinned with a tag other than `latest` or with a digest must still be accepted.
- Other namespaces must not be affected.

verification.description: The policy deny-latest-tag and the binding deny-latest-tag-binding exist (Deny)
Images tagged latest or without a tag are rejected in registry-gate
Pods with pinned images are still accepted (credited once latest is rejected)
The policy applies to registry-gate only (credited once latest is rejected)
